note: status=verified means the figure was confirmed via web search during this run (2026-08-23); status=authoritative-series means the series is standard and stable from the cited primary agency, reproduced from knowledge of the series and flagged with confidence in the datasets; status=analyst-interpretation means the entry is an interpretive judgment, not a raw data point.

sources.name: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) — National Income and Product Accounts
sources.note: Real GDP +2.1% in 2025 (annual), Q1 2026 +2.1%, Q2 2026 advance +1.5%. Used for GDP, GDP per capita series.

sources.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics — Consumer Price Index (CPI-U)
Bureau of Labor Statistics — Current Population Survey (unemployment, earnings, participation)
sources.note: Unemployment 4.1% July 2026 (range 4.1-4.5% in 2026); 2020 peak 14.7% (Apr); 1982 peak 10.8%.

sources.name: U.S. Census Bureau — Income and Poverty (CPS ASEC)
sources.note: Real median household income 2024 = $83,730 (2024$), not statistically different from 2023 $82,690; 2019 (pre-pandemic, revised series) $83,260. Poverty rate 2023 11.1%; SPM 2024 ~12.6%.

sources.name: Congressional Budget Office — Budget and Economic Outlook
sources.note: Debt held by public ~100% of GDP FY2025, rising to 120% by 2036 (Feb 2026 baseline); long-term ~175% of GDP by mid-2050s; FY2025 deficit $1.8T (5.8% of GDP); FY2026 projected $1.9T.

sources.name: U.S. Treasury — Fiscal Data / Monthly Treasury Statement
sources.note: FY2025 spending $7.01T (23% of GDP); FY2025 deficit $1.8T; gross debt ~$38.5T end-2025; net interest FY2025 $970B.

sources.name: Federal Reserve — Distributional Financial Accounts (DFA)
Saez & Zucman — Wealth and income concentration series
sources.note: Top 1% wealth share ~25-30% (1980) rising to ~40-42% (recent); top 1% income share ~10-11% (1980) to ~19-21% (recent). Higher than DFA due to offshore wealth and different valuation of pensions. Report uses ranges.

sources.name: CDC/NCHS — Mortality, Life Expectancy, NVSS
sources.note: Life expectancy 2024 = 79.0 (record high; +0.6 from 2023); men 75.8, women 81.4. 2020: 77.0; 2021: 76.4; 2019: 78.8. Drug overdose deaths peaked ~112k (2023), declined 2024-25.

sources.name: CMS — National Health Expenditure Accounts
Freedom House — Freedom in the World
sources.note: US score: ~94 (2010s) → 83 (2025 report) → 81 (2026 report, covering 2025; sharpest decline of any Free country). Status remains 'Free'. Freedom on the Net US 73/100.

sources.name: V-Dem Institute — Liberal Democracy Index (v2x_libdem)
sources.note: US LDI 0.75 (2024) → 0.57 (2025), -24% in one year, lowest since 1965, ranked 51st (Democracy Report 2026, V-Dem v16).

sources.name: Economist Intelligence Unit — Democracy Index
sources.note: US 2025: 7.65/10, ranked 34th, 'flawed democracy' — lowest since index began (2006). Was 8.16 (2015), 7.98 (2016), ~7.85 (2017-2024).

sources.name: Pew Research Center — State of the American Middle Class
sources.note: Share of adults in middle-income households fell 61% (1971) → 51% (2023); middle-class share of aggregate income 62% → 43%.

sources.name: FBI — Uniform Crime Reporting (crime & homicide rates)
sources.note: 2024: violent crime -4.5%, murder -14.9% (rate ~5.0/100k, lowest since 2015); 2025 preliminary: violent crime -9.3%, murder -18.1% (homicide near 75-year low). 2020 spike: homicide 7.8/100k.

sources.name: Bureau of Justice Statistics — Incarceration counts
sources.note: Prisoners ~1.6M (2009 peak, rate 756/100k) → ~1.23M (2023, rate ~545/100k). Declining but historically extreme by OECD standards.

sources.name: OMB — Historical Tables (Budget of the U.S. Government)
sources.note: Deficit/GDP, debt/GDP, revenue & outlay shares by fiscal year; used for admin-level fiscal attribution.

sources.name: CRFB — Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget analyses
sources.note: FY2025 net interest $970B; debt held by public ~99% of GDP end-FY2025; OBBBA (2025) adds ~$2.4T to primary deficits / ~$3.0T to debt over FY2025-34.

sources.name: CBO — Estimated Budgetary Effects of Public Law 119-21 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act)
sources.note: Net +$3.4T to unified deficits FY2025-2034; making TCJA permanent adds ~$858B more. Tax Foundation: revenue reduction ~$5.2T over 10 years.

sources.name: Robert Shiller / Online Data — CAPE (Cyclically Adjusted P/E)
sources.note: CAPE ~40.5-41.6 (Jul-Aug 2026), highest since Aug 2000, second-highest ever (record 44.2 in 1999). Median ~16-17. Long-run mean ~17.

sources.name: Wikipedia — U.S. economic performance by presidential party
sources.note: Real GDP growth averaged ~1.8pp faster under Democrats (≈4.6% vs ≈2.4% annualized, quarterly data). S&P 500 annual gains ~11-13% D vs ~9-10% R (various windows).

sources.name: Investopedia — GDP growth by president
sources.note: Per-president real GDP growth: FDR ~9.3% (recovery), Truman ~1.4%, Eisenhower ~2.9%, Kennedy ~4.4%, Johnson ~5.3%, Nixon ~2.7%, Ford ~1.6%, Carter ~3.0%, Reagan ~3.5%, GHWB ~2.1%, Clinton ~3.9%, GWB ~1.9%, Obama ~1.5%, Trump ~1.3% (incl. COVID), Biden ~3.2% (2021-24).

sources.name: NBER — U.S. Business Cycle Expansions and Contractions
sources.note: Official recession dating. Used for recession overlays and admin-level attribution.

sources.name: OECD — Health Statistics / Life Expectancy
sources.note: US life expectancy ~79 vs peer average ~82-84; US infant & maternal mortality far above peers; US spending highest (~18% GDP vs ~10-12% peers).

sources.name: HUD — Annual Homeless Assessment Report (AHAR)
sources.note: ~653k (2023) → ~771k (2024), record highs; 2025 ~895k (estimates). Rising sharply since 2020.

sources.name: World Inequality Database (WID.world)
sources.note: Income and wealth concentration series; used alongside Fed DFA with explicit range reporting.

sources.name: Polity 5 Project — Polity 2 score
sources.note: US consistently scored 10 (full democracy) in modern era; less sensitive than V-Dem/EIU to recent changes.

sources.name: Gallup — Trust in Government / Institutions
sources.note: Trust in federal government 'to do what is right' ~20-25% range since ~2007 (from ~70-80% in 1960s). Congress approval ~20-30%.

sources.name: Federal Reserve — Federal Funds Rate history
sources.note: Fed funds 3.50-3.75% (July 2026), held 5 consecutive meetings; three 25bp cuts in 2025. Peak 5.25-5.50% (2023-24); 1981 peak ~20% (Volcker); 2020 emergency cuts to 0-0.25%.

sources.name: Hensel & Ziemba — 'The Stock Market and Presidential Elections' / Hensel (1995)
sources.note: Found small-cap and large-cap returns significantly higher under Democratic administrations; caveats about sample size and timing.

sources.name: C-SPAN — Presidential Historians Survey 2021
sources.note: James Buchanan ranked 44th of 44 (last) in 2021; Trump 41st in 2021 but last (44th) in the 2017 edition, displacing Buchanan at the bottom. Rankings are subjective scholarly judgment, not economic measures.

sources.name: APSA Presidential Greatness Project 2024 / Siena College Research Institute 2022
sources.note: APSA 2024: Trump ranked last (45th, 10.9/100), Buchanan 44th (16.7), Johnson 43rd. Siena 2022: Johnson 45th, Buchanan 44th, Trump 43rd of 45. Historian rankings are subjective judgments, not economic measures.
